ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A voltage commutation circuit is shown in the image. If the turn-off time of the SCR is 50 μsec and a safety margin of 2 is considered, then what will be the approximate minimum value of capacitor required for proper commutation?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a voltage commutation circuit, with a 100 V DC power supply on the left; between the upper and lower buses there are two branches, each branch has a 50 Ω resistor above, and below are thyristors Th1 and Th2 respectively; capacitor C is connected between the middle nodes between the two 50 Ω resistors and the corresponding thyristors. Reasoning: This structure corresponds to a complementary voltage commutation circuit. The turn-off time tq of the SCR = 50 μs, and the safety factor is 2, therefore the required commutation time tc = 2 × 50 μs = 100 μs. According to the specified relation tc = R C ln 2, taking R = 50 Ω, then C = tc / (R ln 2) = 100×10^-6 / (50×0.693) F ≈ 2.88×10^-6 F. Therefore the approximate minimum value of the required capacitor is 2.88 μF.

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram and identify the complementary voltage commutation circuit: two equal 50 Ω resistors feed the SCR anode nodes and capacitor C is connected between those nodes. From the question, take SCR turn-off time t_q = 50 μs and safety margin = 2, so required commutation time is t_c = 2 × 50 μs = 100 μs. Apply the standard relation t_c = R C ln 2 with R = 50 Ω. Solve C = 100 μs /(50 ln 2) ≈ 2.88 × 10^-6 F, so the minimum capacitor is about 2.88 μF.

method.method_draft: Begin by describing the diagram: a 100 V source supplies two identical branches, each having a 50 Ω resistor above an SCR, and capacitor C bridges the two SCR anode nodes. Consider the instant the conducting SCR is to be commutated by firing the other SCR. The capacitor voltage gives reverse bias to the outgoing SCR, and the reverse-bias duration is the time until the outgoing anode node returns to zero. Model the midpoint voltage as the first-order response v(t)=V_s(1-2e^{-t/(50C)}). The reverse bias ends when v(t)=0, giving t=50C ln2. The required t is the turn-off time times safety margin, 50 μs × 2 = 100 μs. Therefore C = 100 μs/(50 ln2) ≈ 2.88 μF.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For this voltage commutation action, the capacitor is initially charged approximately to the supply voltage with polarity opposite for the next commutation. After the alternate SCR is triggered, the outgoing SCR remains reverse biased until its anode voltage rises back to zero. The first-order waveform can be written in normalized form as v(t) = V_s(1 - 2e^{-t/(RC)}); setting v(t)=0 gives e^{-t/(RC)}=1/2, hence t = RC ln 2. Then enforce the safety-factor-adjusted turn-off time.
